q-35972.name: Question 1
q-35972.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $M(-1,-2,-3)$ and $N(2,3,4).$
q-35972.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $M$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=m+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $m$ is the position vector of $M.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $M(-1,-2,-3)$ and $N(2,3,4)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{MN} \\  & =⟨2,3,4⟩-⟨-1,-2,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,5,7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

q-69807.name: Question 2
q-69807.problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(3,2,1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩.$ Find all the possible points $Y$ on that line such that $YP=\sqrt{160}.$
q-69807.worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩+t⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Since $Y$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OY} & =⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩+t⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PY} & =\overset{\to }{OY}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩+t⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩)-⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩ \\  & =t⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨t,\,3t,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PY=\sqrt{160},$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}YP & =\sqrt{160} \\ |\overset{\to }{PY}| & =\sqrt{160} \\ |⟨t,\,3t,\,0⟩| & =\sqrt{160} \\ \sqrt{{t}^{2}+(3t)^{2}+{0}^{2}} & =\sqrt{160} \\ \sqrt{10{t}^{2}} & =\sqrt{160} \\ \pm \sqrt{10}t & =4\sqrt{10} \\ t & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm 4$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{Y}_{1}}=⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩+4⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩=⟨7,14,1⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{Y}_{2}}=⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩-4⟨1,\,3,\,0⟩=⟨-1,-10,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are ${Y}_{1}(7,14,1)$ and ${Y}_{2}(-1,-10,1).$

and

PY→=OY→−OP→=(⟨3,2,1⟩+t⟨1,3,0⟩)−⟨3,2,1⟩=t⟨1,3,0⟩=⟨t,3t,0⟩.

q-126432.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $A(2,-3,5)$ and $B(3,1,-2).$
q-126432.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $A$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=a+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $a$ is the position vector of $A.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $A(2,-3,5)$ and $B(3,1,-2)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{AB} \\  & =⟨3,1,-2⟩-⟨2,-3,5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,4,-7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -7\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

q-126965.problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(3,3,1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-4,-2,4⟩.$ Find all the possible points $A$ on that line such that $AP=3.$
q-126965.worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨3,3,1⟩+t⟨-4,-2,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Since $A$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OA} & =⟨3,3,1⟩+t⟨-4,-2,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PA} & =\overset{\to }{OA}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨3,3,1⟩+t⟨-4,-2,4⟩)-⟨3,3,1⟩ \\  & =t\,⟨-4,-2,4⟩ \\  & =⟨-4t,\,-2t,\,4t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PA=3,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}AP & =3 \\ |\overset{\to }{PA}| & =3 \\ |⟨-4t,\,-2t,\,4t⟩| & =3 \\ \sqrt{(-4t)^{2}+(-2t)^{2}+(4t)^{2}} & =3 \\ \sqrt{16{t}^{2}+4{t}^{2}+16{t}^{2}} & =3 \\ \sqrt{36{t}^{2}} & =3 \\ \pm 6t & =3 \\ t & =\pm \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm \frac{1}{2}$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{1}}=⟨3,3,1⟩+\frac{1}{2}⟨-4,-2,4⟩=⟨1,2,3⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{2}}=⟨3,3,1⟩-\frac{1}{2}⟨-4,-2,4⟩=⟨5,4,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are ${A}_{1}(1,2,3)$ and ${A}_{2}(5,4,-1).$

$$

What is the value of $a+b+c?$
q-162163.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
r=p+tv\,⟹\,r=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$

and the vector equation of the  line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ is

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,t\in [0,1].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=2+7+0=9.
$$
